# Building the test world

This guide covers exactly what you must have set up before the GameTests can run — and the
checks that no automatic test can perform.

## Short version

**You do not have to build anything.** The structure template is generated by a script:

```
powershell -File tools/make_gametest_structure.ps1
```

This writes `solar_platform.nbt` for all three targets — a platform of 16 × 8 × 9 with a
bedrock floor at level 0 and air above it. The files are checked in; you only need the
script if the size should change.

Then directly:

```
gradlew :neoforge:1211:runGameTestServer
```

> **Correction to an earlier statement of mine:** I had written that a `.nbt` cannot be
> generated from code. That is not true — the format is gzip-compressed NBT with size,
> block palette and position list, and for an empty platform it is written in a few lines.
> The manual build below remains only as a reference, in case you ever need an arena with
> real content.

What you **really** have to check manually is part 3: the SU bug on restart. No GameTest
can run that.

---

## Part 1: Building the structure template by hand (reference only)

Not needed for `solar_platform` — see the short version. This guide is for the case that you
later need an arena with prebuilt blocks.

> **By the way:** `/test create` already creates the floor itself, from bedrock across the
> full base area. You do not have to place blocks by hand for that.

### 1. Start the dev client

```
gradlew :neoforge:1211:runClient
```

This automatically opens the world `CPM Testwork`.

### 2. Find free space

```
/gamemode creative
```

Important: **nothing above the build site.** No roof, no trees, no overhangs, no mountain
next to it that reaches in.

Why this is so critical: `canSeeSky()` is in fact a sky-light query —

```java
default boolean canSeeSky(BlockPos pos) {
    return this.getBrightness(LightLayer.SKY, pos) >= this.getMaxLightLevel();
}
```

If anything is above, the sky light is below 15 and **every** solar test reports "generates
nothing". The test `generatesUnderOpenSky` checks this first and tells you so explicitly.
If it fails: rebuild the template, do not adjust the expectations.

### 3. Create the area

```
/test create solar_platform 16 8 9
```

16 long (X), 8 high (Y), 9 wide (Z). The length of 16 is not a coincidence — the shading tests
of the horizontal generator need a clear path of 11 blocks in front of the panel so that
"distance 11 has no effect anymore" can be checked too.

### 4. Lay the floor

Fill **only the bottom layer** (relative height 0) completely with stone.
16 × 9 = 144 blocks.

Everything above stays **air**. In the test, the generators stand at height 1.

### 5. Save

Right-click the structure block, mode "Save". Enter in "Structure Name":

```
createphotomovement:solar_platform
```

Then **SAVE**.

### 6. Copy the file

The export goes to:

```
neoforge/1211/run/saves/CPM Testwork/generated/createphotomovement/structures/solar_platform.nbt
```

Copy it to:

```
neoforge/1211/src/main/resources/data/createphotomovement/structure/solar_platform.nbt
```

> **Pitfall:** The export folder is called `structures` (plural), but the resource folder in
> 1.21.1 is `structure` (singular). When porting later to 1.20.1 and Fabric, the resource
> folder there is called `structures` again.

### 7. Run it

```
gradlew :neoforge:1211:runGameTestServer
```

## Part 2: What the GameTests cover

According to your scenario list, split by what can be automated.

### Solar generator and advanced solar generator

| Scenario | Automated |
|---|---|
| Open sky → generates | ✅ |
| Stone above → does not generate | ✅ |
| Glass above → keeps generating | ✅ |
| Carpet / snow layer above → does not generate | ✅ |
| Night → does not generate | ✅ |
| Rain → half speed | ❌ **cannot be produced in the arena**, see below |
| Advanced yields more than base | ✅ |
| Colored variant behaves like uncolored | ✅ |
| SU stays the same at night → day → night | ✅ |
| SU stays the same after game restart | ❌ **manual**, see part 3 |

### Horizontal and advanced horizontal solar generator

| Scenario | Automated |
|---|---|
| Open sky → generates | ✅ |
| Night → does not generate | ✅ |
| Block **directly** in front → does not generate | ✅ |
| Block at distance 2 → reduced | ✅ |
| Block at distance 8 (gap of 7) → reduced | ✅ |
| Block at distance 11 → **no effect** anymore | ✅ |
| Glass in front → does not block | ✅ |
| Glass at distance 8 → does not reduce | ✅ |
| Sun path curve: east high in the morning, low in the evening | ✅ |
| Sun path curve: west the reverse | ✅ |
| North/south always at minimum | ✅ |
| Advanced multiplier correct | ✅ |
| SU stays the same after game restart | ❌ **manual**, see part 3 |

### Solar windmill bearing

Compares throughout against a second, identical bearing with Create's ordinary sails, placed
right next to it.

| Scenario | Automated |
|---|---|
| 9 solar sails assemble, are counted as solar | ✅ |
| Create's sails are counted as regular | ✅ |
| Day, open sky → ×2.0 SU | ✅ |
| Sail type does **not** change the speed | ✅ |
| Covered → ×1.0, **but keeps turning** | ✅ |
| **Night → keeps turning**, same speed as the reference | ✅ |
| Night → ×1.0 | ✅ |
| Rain → ×1.5 | ✅ **rain works here**, see below |
| Thunderstorm → ×1.0, keeps turning | ✅ |
| Network SU unchanged after two day-night cycles | ✅ |
| Speed exactly the same over day → night → day | ✅ |
| After disassembly 0 RPM and 0 SU | ✅ |
| SU stays the same after game restart | ❌ **manual**, see part 3 |

### Why rain is not a GameTest

The generator reads `level.isRainingAt(pos)`. That checks not only whether it is raining,
but also whether the MOTION_BLOCKING heightmap lies **above** the position — and in a GameTest
arena it always does. Measured in this arena:

```
raining=true, rainLevel=0.60, precipitation=RAIN, canSeeSky=true,
heightmapY=-50, posY=-57   ->   isRainingAt=false
```

So it is raining, the biome fits, the sky is open — and Minecraft still considers the position
covered. No matter where in the arena the panel stands.

The halving itself is covered by `SolarGeneratorOutputTest.basicRain` and `advancedRain`; in
the world code it depends on a single `isRainingAt` call. It can only really be verified by
hand — **check F** below.

**With the windmill bearing it is different, and there rain is automated.** The bearing asks
`level.isRaining()` — the global weather, without location reference and without heightmap.
Same weather, a different question. Only the panels trip over the arena.

Incidentally: weather does not take effect in Minecraft immediately. The switches are set
instantly, but two intensity values are read which move toward their target by 0.01 per tick —
`isRaining()` requires more than 0.2, `isThundering()` more than 0.9. A thunderstorm therefore
needs about 90 ticks. For the manual checks this means: after `/weather rain`, wait about five
seconds before reading the value.

### How the shading really calculates

Decided on 2026-08-01: **it stays at the fixed minimum value**, no halving.

| Situation | SU per RPM (base capacity 16) |
|---|---|
| East, dawn, clear | 64 |
| East, noon, clear | 22 |
| East, dusk, clear | 8 |
| West, dawn, clear | 8 |
| West, dusk, clear | 64 |
| North or south, always | 8 |
| **Covered (distance 2–10), no matter when or where** | **8** |
| Block directly in front (distance 1) | **0 — generates nothing** |

A covered generator therefore delivers the minimum value, not half. Anyone who reads
"reduced" while playing should expect this.

### What "transparent" means technically

The shading test uses `getLightBlock(...) > 0`:

```java
if (state.isSolidRender(level, pos)) return 15;      // stone, wood, wool -> blocks
else return state.propagatesSkylightDown(...) ? 0 : 1;
```

- **Clear glass, glass panes** → 0 → does **not** block
- **Stone and everything solid** → 15 → blocks
- **Tinted glass, leaves, ice, water** → 1 → blocks

So tinted glass blocks, clear glass does not. This is intended and is tested.

## Part 3: Manual checklist — the SU bug on restart

A GameTest cannot restart the server. These checks must be done in the client. It is the bug
that, according to the changelog, occurred in an earlier version: **the produced SU added up
on load instead of staying the same.**

### Setup

1. World `CPM Testwork`, open sky, daytime.
2. Place a solar generator, attach a shaft, and connect a stress meter (stressometer) to the network.
3. Note the value.

### Check A — reload chunk

1. Note the SU value.
2. Walk far away until the chunk unloads (or F3 + A is not enough — really far, > 10 chunks).
3. Come back.
4. **Expectation:** the same value. Not double.

### Check B — leave the world and reload it

1. Note the SU value.
2. Save and leave the world, then load it again.
3. **Expectation:** the same value.

### Check C — completely restart the game

1. Note the SU value.
2. Quit Minecraft, restart `runClient`, load the world.
3. **Expectation:** the same value.

### Check D — day-night change over several cycles

1. `/time set day`, note the value.
2. `/time set night` → expectation: generator stands still, SU drops to 0.
3. `/time set day` → **expectation: exactly the value from step 1.** Not more.
4. Repeat three to four times. If the value rises every cycle, the bug is back.

### Check E — the same with the windmill bearing

Build a solar-sail contraption, then repeat A to D.

Only the **restart part** remains. Everything else on the bearing is now automated: night,
rain, thunderstorm, covering, disassembly and two day-night cycles are checked by
`SolarWindmillGameTests`. What that does not cover is exactly reloading from disk.

If you are interested while building: **at night the bearing must keep turning** — only the
solar bonus drops away. A standstill would be an error.

### Check F — rain and thunder

Only needed for the **panels**; for the windmill bearing, rain is automated (×1.5) and
thunder likewise (×1.0).

After each `/weather` command **wait about five seconds** — the weather intensity moves toward
its target by 0.01 per tick, and a thunderstorm needs roughly 90 ticks before the game counts it
as one. If you read the value immediately, you measure the old state.

1. Daytime, open sky, solar generator running. Note the speed (default: 16 RPM).
2. `/weather rain`, wait → **expectation: half speed** (8 RPM).
3. `/weather thunder`, wait → expectation: likewise halved.
4. `/weather clear`, wait → back to the starting value. Not above it.

With the horizontal generator the same applies; there the rain counts on the block **in front**
of the panel, not above it.

### If a check fails

Note **which** check and **by which factor** the value is off (doubled? does the starting value
add up each time?). This narrows it down immediately: the suspicious place is
`SolarWindmillBearingBlockEntity.initialize()` and `onNetworkChange()`, where `initFromTE()`
counts the capacity both as `unloadedCapacity` and via the source list. For the horizontal
generators it is `calculateAddedStressCapacity()` together with `lastCapacityProvided`.

There is also an open drift between the targets there, which I deliberately did not touch —
see `docs/common-code-analysis.md`, section "Still open". Results from this checklist decide
which variant wins.
